title: Canary anchor eval and safe apply for batching/caching recommendations
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a conservative canary-and-anchor evaluation harness that validates automated batching/caching configuration recommendations before applying them to production. The goal is to detect subtle quality regressions tied to cost-saving changes (batch size increases, aggressive prefix/KV caching, quantization-adjacent kernel choices) and to provide a deterministic accept/reject signal to the config-apply automation. This task covers evaluation corpus curation (anchor prompts), statistical tests, rollout gating logic, safe rollback flow, and observability hooks for post-apply monitoring.
acceptance_criteria: Create an anchor prompt set (~120 prompts) that covers instruction-following, long-context reasoning, multi-turn state, and hallucination probes.
Implement automated A/B evaluation comparing baseline vs recommended config using embedding-similarity and task-specific pass/fail checks.
Define reject thresholds for primary metrics (semantic-similarity delta, instruction-accuracy drop, hallucination-rate increase) with at least 95% confidence using bootstrap CI.
Integrate the canary harness with the autotune pipeline: shadow run -> canary (1% traffic) -> progressive rollout with automated rollback on breach.
Add dashboards and alerting for regression signals and expose a one-click manual rollback in the Console.
Document runbook and attach a postmortem template for any regression-triggered rollback events.
implementation_plan: Week 1: Curate anchor corpus from production prompts, QA team picks edge cases and known failure modes.
Week 2: Build evaluation runner in CI that executes baseline vs candidate for the anchor set and computes metrics (embedding cosine delta, exact-match for structured outputs, hallucination probes).
Week 3: Add statistical gate logic (bootstrap CIs, effect-size threshold) and integrate with autotune's staging apply path.
Week 4: Wire Console dashboards and alerting; create canary rollout orchestration and rollback hooks in orchestration service.
Week 5: Run internal dogfood, collect telemetry, iterate thresholds, and publish runbook.
progress_updates: 2026-02-22: Kickoff meeting with PM and QA. Agreed on anchor prompt taxonomy and target domains (search-rerank, summarization, code generation safety cases).
2026-02-26: Initial anchor set (60 prompts) assembled from anonymized prod traces + curated stress cases from QA. Stored in gs://redwood-anchor/ENG-50321/v1.

2026-03-02: Prototype eval runner merged to feature branch (PR #5823). Embedding-based similarity and token-level edit distance metrics implemented. These run in ~9s per prompt on CI infra with batching disabled.
2026-03-06: Early results showed a 0.7% average semantic-similarity drop for a recommended batch increase for one model; PM requested tightening thresholds and adding instruction-accuracy checks.

2026-03-10: Added instruction-following binary checks and hallucination probes; updated evaluation to compute bootstrap CIs. Discovered a false-positive signal from prompts with heavy personalization — filtered those from anchor set.
decisions: Use embedding-cosine delta as the primary continuous metric and instruction-accuracy as a binary safety metric.
Require both (a) semantic-similarity drop < 1.0% (95% bootstrap CI) AND (b) instruction-accuracy drop <= 0.5 percentage points for an automated accept.
Start canary at 1% user traffic for 24 hours, progressive increase to 5% then 25% if no regression signals are observed.
Automated rollback if any metric breaches thresholds with at least 95% confidence and sustained signal for 30 minutes.
risks_mitigations: Risk: Anchor set may not reflect edge user behavior -> Mitigation: weekly refresh pipeline to sample production prompts and add failing cases.
Risk: Small effect sizes may be noisy -> Mitigation: use bootstrap CI and enforce minimum sample size; prefer conservative thresholds for first rollout.
Risk: Eval runner changes runtime performance of candidate -> Mitigation: run eval in shadow mode and compare latency separately, do not conflate latency with quality metrics.
test_corpus_summary: Anchor corpus v1: 120 prompts, balanced across domains: 30 summarization/compression, 30 multi-turn dialog, 30 code editing/code generation, 30 factual consistency/hallucination probes. Each prompt includes a golden answer or success predicate where applicable and a set of variant paraphrases to detect brittleness.
rollback_policy: If any primary metric breaches the defined threshold with 95% CI sustained for 30 minutes during canary or progressive rollout, the orchestrator will automatically revert to the last known-good config, invalidate affected cache entries if applicable, and create a regression incident with telemetry snapshot and links to diffs. Manual override option available in Console with justification required.
playbook_todo: Triage the regression: compare per-prompt diffs between baseline and candidate, identify pattern (edge case, tokenizer-induced, quantization artifact).
If regression is due to batching/caching ordering, attempt non-invasive mitigation: reduce batch window, disable prefix caching for affected route.
If regression persists, escalate to ML infra and model owners; capture heap of KV cache for reproducer and open a reproducible test in CI.
Run mitigations in staging, replay failing traces, and only reapply candidate when anchor eval passes and dogfood metrics are stable for 48 hours.
notes: Avoid using single-metric gates (e.g., only embedding delta) — combined checks reduce false accepts.
We should coordinate with Sales for customers on Dedicated where aggressive caching is proposed; add an opt-out flag per customer for autotune.
Next step: run a 2-week canary on non-critical routes to calibrate thresholds before enabling on higher-traffic routes.
